raw_comment:
Lebron James Breaks Records With His Career Points in 2023. 

Lebron James has the highest career points out of anyone else featured on the graph. His points have reached 38,390, the next closest player (Kareem Abdul-Jabbar) only reached 38,387. Though these points are close, Labron is still the highest out of all 250.  On the x-axis of the graph is the player's age, and the y-axis has how many careers points the player has gained while in the NBA. The graph also uses a purple color to differentiate between players that are currently in the league vs previous NBA players. The graph also includes only the top 250 scorers. This graph can help current players in the NBA keep track of how their career points compare to other players, and how their trajectory compares. This can also apply to basketball players in our community at Eden Prairie High School. We wonder who collects the data and how they keep track of the data. How do they judge what specifically is a career point? How will Labron’s career look after he finally retires?

raw_comment:
What do you notice? If your notice makes a claim, where in the graph is the evidence to support it?
I noticed that LeBron James began his professional career at a young age and rose to the top of the game by the time he was 38. LeBron James has advanced faster and more effectively than other players while also being younger than the majority of other basketball players. He has outperformed all other players in terms of what he has accomplished at a young age. We can also see that LeBron's line is steeper than the lines of the other players, showing that he has accrued more points in a shorter amount of time.

What do you wonder?
I wonder if his early career start helped him improve or if he had unique opportunities than all the other players that allowed him to make progress more quickly than others. We know that the longer you play, the better you get but Lebron seems to be earning more points at an earlier age than the rest, I wonder why ? 

How does this relate to you and your community?
Even though I personally don't watch or have an interest about basketball, some of my peers do. If they want to pursue the same career path, they can observe him and learn from him. especially if others look to him as a role model.

raw_comment:
1. The first thing I notice is that LeBron James has overpassed the previous record holder for career points, Kareem Abdul Jabbar. LeBron also surpassed Kareem by beating his lifetime career points nearly 4 years earlier. If we take a closer look at LeBron james has been demolishing the competition by being consistently higher in lifetime career points for the people of his age, he has always been at the top of the game. I also notice that there are these points in time where the line stays stagnant and then gets a surge in points, and as age increases those boost in points decrease. 

2. I wonder what makes the patterns of these graphs, for example if we compare LeBron James to Kobe Bryant there's clearly a similarity in the pattern. Both lines seem to rise and stay stagnant at nearly the same time, is it the basketball season that impacts this, if so why do some players have longer breaks than others?

3. This relates to my community because no one really knows who can be the next LeBron James. A great basketball player can come from anywhere. In my town there are many young people who share an interest in basketball and it is just surreal to see that a potential pro-athlete can be one of them

4.  "LeBron James, The Record Breaking Superstar!"

raw_comment:
I notice that Lebron James started off at a young age and throughout his whole career he has been the player with the most points. His line is steeper than everyone else's including Kareem who was the previous title winner. Lebron was able to break the record at an earlier age compared to Kareem, around a 5 year difference. Also, I notice that players that started off young are most likely to have more career points than the ones that started later on.

I wonder how and what could have helped Lebron score the most points throughout his whole career? What did he do to train, who trained him, how much did he train, and did he just have more opportunities? Could it have been that starting at a younger age helped get the title at an earlier age. 

This relates to me and my community because I know there are many basketball and Lebron fans that look up to him. Also, many would want to become one of those players and I think this inspires them to be better, and probably train from a younger age.

raw_comment:
1. I see that no player has yet exceeded the top score in this graph, which is 40,000 career points. The closest to 40,000 points are Lebron James (38,390) and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar (38,387).  On addition to having a better score, LeBron also has a more linear graph and achieved this earlier in his life (38 years old) than Kareem (41 years old). The most frequent scores are around 5,000 to 20,000 points.

2. I wonder if any future basketball players will surpass LeBron's scoring record that was previously held for 38 years. The game of basketball has changed incredibly over the years and the competition is just getting better and better.  As someone who has been playing basketball since I was 4 years old, I understand the game and am truly amazed at how Lebron broke this unbelievable record. If anyone ever breaks it in the future, it will not be easy.  However, given that LeBron James put in a lot of hardwork and dedication to score 38,390 points in his career, I question whether this will actually occur.

3. This relates to me because I have been playing basketball since I was 4 years old and am a big fan of Lebron. He is an inspiration and is definitely one of the best athletes of all time. I personally have seen a lot of his games and actually watched him break the record on TV. 

4. Lebron James: The King Conquers Scoring

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
I noticed that the slope of Lebron James lines is substantially steeper, showing that he scored more points per game on average than Kareem Abdul-Jabbar did. LeBron and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar both have identical overall scoring totals, however Abdul-Jabbar didn't catch up to LeBron until he was about 42 years old. One can see  that from his rookie season to year 20, Lebron has been the most consistent scorer.

What do you wonder?
When Lebron reaches the same age as Kareem from the moment in his career when he scored the most points, I wonder what his point average will be. I also wonder if the players on your squad have any bearing on your ability to score points. Lebron and Kareem were receiving assists and support from others, so they weren't scoring all by themselves. I'm curious to know if their scoring streaks reduced after being traded or switched to different teams.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This is relevant to my town because many young people in my city aspire to play in the NBA, and it demonstrates that you can surpass the scoring leader you were raised knowing if you put in a lot of effort and dedication. It relates to my generation and how we are innovating and growing younger while achieving goals that others who came before us accomplished at a more older age.

What’s going on in this graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

"Eyes on the Net and a Double Threat"

raw_comment:
1.) One thing I noticed is that LeBron James is now the NBA's all -time leading scorer. This is crazy to think about, as I have watched LeBron James almost half of his career, and have watched him play since I became a serious basketball fan in 2015. Another thing I noticed is that Rudy Gay is on this list. It's interesting because the graph claims he hit 17,500 points at age 36, and he is 36 right now. Rudy Gay is only currently averaging 4.8 points per game for a struggling Utah Jazz team, and is not playing too many minutes per game (15 on a good night). The point I'm trying to drive home, is that you wouldn't expect to see Gay on a list with LeBron, Michael Jordan, Kobe, Curry, etc. I also remember the night LeBron passed Kobe. It was an exciting night, but tragedy ensued the next morning when Kobe Bryant unfortunately passed away at everyone's surprise.

2.) I wonder where Russell Westbrook lands on this list. He was a really good second fiddle to Kevin Durant for awhile in OKC, and then was their leading scorer for a couple of years. I also wonder if anyone will ever break LeBron's scoring record (My guess is Luka Doncic or Victor Wembanyama IF it happens).

3.) This has an impact on me and my community because a lot of people from my town watch basketball. Even people from my Stats class watch it, such as my great teacher Mr. Hibino and some classmates such as Charlie and Enzo.

4.) Catchy title: LeScoringTitle

raw_comment:
What do you notice? 

I notice that LeBron James outscored the top 250 scores at almost all ages from 20 and up. I have noticed that there are areas in all of the lines where they are not accruing points. Lebron James' high total was attained roughly six years before the previous titleholder; his lines' slope is also much steeper, indicating that he averaged more points per game than Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Lebron James' career began much earlier than that of many other players, and when combined with his talent, he became a contender to hold the NBA record for most points scored.

What do you wonder? 

I wonder why LeBron James is/was able to score more than all other players. Was it his athleticism, and skills or did competition get easier allowing him to score more? I wonder if LeBron will retain his title as the top scorer or would somebody in the future come along and dethrone him from that title. 

How does this relate to you or your community? 

This relates to me and my community as we are both minorities and play a sport. LeBron has made major achievements in his athletic field and while mine aren't as great I have to by winning several awards and being in articles.

raw_comment:
Thanks to all students who responded.   In New Jersey, there is either LeBron fever, a love of basketball or excellence in writing headlines, but six of the seven great headlines are from the Garden State.  
Here are some of the catchy headlines that we received:  "Lebron James: The Young NBA Career Scoring Leader” by Gabe of Auburn High School in Massachusetts; “LeBron James: Youngest with Most Career Points” by Colleen of Academy of Saint Elizabeth in Morristown, New Jersey; three from students at Perth Amboy High School in New Jersey -- “King James Reigns Supreme Amongst NBA’s Elite: Top 250 Scorers Announced!” by Cesar, "LeBron James Sweeps the Court: Will He Stay on Top?" by Alida, and “LeBron’s Journey to Becoming a Legend” by Michelle and two from New Jersey (no school name given) “LeBron James Shoots His Way Past Abdul-Jabbar and Straight Into History” by Kaitlin and “New King in Town: LeBron Takes the Crown for Highest Career Points” by Isabella.
You can continue to post responses.  Please check back by Friday, Feb. 17 to see the Reveal with the free link to the original New York Times article with its six graphs, some questions about this graph and a few Stat Nuggets.
The next “What’s Going On In This Graph?” will be released by Friday, Feb. 17 with moderation on Wednesday, March 1.  The topic – the earthquake affecting Turkey and Syria.    
Signing off – Sharon Hessney from Boston, who marvels in sports that she cannot do, and Wendy Clark in Idaho cheering you on!

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
From looking at this graph, I noticed that LeBron James is the youngest player to be in the top 250 scorers. In 2023, he held 38,390 career points. 
 
What do you wonder?
From looking at this graph, I wonder how different combinations of teams affect how many points an athlete can obtain. 


What’s going on in this graph?
This graph depicts different NBA players and how many career points they have obtained over the years. The main player is LeBron James, since he has just recently become the NBA career scoring leader, however, basketball legends such as Kobe Bryan and Micheal Jordan are also depicted. 


How does this relate to you and your community?
This graph relates to my community, more than myself, since I don’t personally watch much basketball. However, my brother and father both watch basketball and would find this graph extremely entertaining.

raw_comment:
I notice that in all of the lines there are plateaus where they are not scoring points, this is likely due to off seasons where they can't add to their lifetime point total. I noticed that Lebron James' high total was achieved about 6 years before the past holder of the title, his lines slope is a lot steeper, which means he had a higher average of points scored per game than Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Lebron James' career also started a lot earlier than a lot of other players, that paired with his skill put him as a contender of holding the highest point total in the NBA. 

I wonder what Lebron's point total is going to be at the end of his time playing for the NBA. If he keeps playing to or past Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, and his avg. points per game don't vastly decrease, then he should in theory be scoring to or past 40,000 points. If this happens, then I wonder who the next person to beat the record will be and when they start playing professionally, if rules were to change or if someone with a high enough skill level were to start playing before Lebron did, then would they be able to beat the record? I also wonder if it will take another 34 or more years to beat Lebron James' new record, and by how much it'll be beaten.

Lebron James is a man of color who has inspired many people, all across the world, but he resonates in the hearts of young black boys everywhere, who see him as a role model. Many people in my community love him.

"Career Point Totals Reveal the king of the Court."

raw_comment: This graph demonstrates the NBA's top 250 scorers because this past week, LeBron James broke the scoring record.  The previous scoring record of 38,387 points was held by Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.  The main thing I noticed is how LeBron James reached this high amount of points at a younger age in comparison to the last record holder.  He reached 38,390 points by the time he was 38 years old.  Abdul-Jabbar did not reach his point total until he was 42.  I wonder what other factors play into these results.  Did they suffer any injuries that stopped them from earning more points? How many games did it take them to reach these totals?  This relates to me and my community because many people are fans of the NBA, and specifically LeBron James.  It is also interesting to watch history be created.  I would entitle this graph: "Record Breaking Scoring."

raw_comment:
This graph represents the top 250 scorers of the NBA according to age. The purple represents the current players and the gray represents those who are retired.

I wonder if LeBron James beginning his career so young contributed to him breaking the record?

I observe that LeBron James had the sharpest slope compared to any other player. This means that he was able to accumulate the most points in the least amount of time. The longest careers also seem to correlate to the  highest career scores. This makes sense since the longer that people are allowed to play, the most points they are able to accumulate. 

This relates to me and my community, as the graph seems to show that starting a career in professional sports young, can lead to being successful.

Headline: The Rise of NBA Stars

raw_comment:
What do I notice? 
- LeBron's points were nearly the same as Kevin Durant at the very beginning of their careers. 
- Kareem Abdul-Jabbar has similar overall points as LeBron, but it took Abdul-Jabbar until around age 42 to reach where LeBron is at around 38. 
- There are very few current players compared to the many others on the graph. 
What do I wonder? 
- What helped LeBron in his training become so successful regarding points? 
- How long, on average, does it take most players to reach near the career points LeBron has? 
- Does how many points LeBron has scored have to do with his relatively long career? 
What do I think is going on in this graph? 
- I think this graph is exhibiting basketball player, LeBron James's, overall career points up to age around age 38. The graph also shows the records of other players, both current and retired. This graph highlights other famous names such as Kobe Bryant and Kevin Durant. 
How does this relate to you and your community? 
- This relates to me and my community because, despite not knowing too much about basketball, many people around me know about James's record and other players on this graph. This graph exhibits the little knowledge myself and those around me have about basketball--that being that James and other noted players on the graph are very, very good. 
- Title: "LeBron is Leading the Score"

raw_comment:
I noticed that most of the players started between the ages 20-24 and roughly all the lines are moderately linear with some being a bit curved. The graph shows that those that started at a younger age are able to score more points than those that started after 22.

I wonder if another reason for younger players being able to score more career points could have to do with older experienced players retiring. Could the increase in older professionals retiring affect the career points of the players?

This relates to my community as it could inspire someone to want to play a sport professionally at a young age. Younger kids could see this graph and be motivated to train in a sport they like as they could be really good in their future.

Up and Coming NBA Stars

1. As Karl Malone and Kareem were much older in their later years and not in their prime, I notice that Lebron's rate of points and age is higher than any other player's. It is fair to say that Lebron has been the most consistent in gaining points from his rookie year to year 20. raw_comment:
I notice that the older the players get, the higher career points they have scored. However, Lebron James not only became the career scoring leader, but the youngest to reach 38, 390 career points at the age of 38. I also notice that it has been over 30 years  since someone has reached this number of points. Karl Malone is the only player to come close to beating Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's record in 1989. 
I wonder how many points they average each season to reach this many career points. I also wonder at what age Kareem reached this record compared to Lebron James and how long he had been playing for. Since Lebron James is so young still, I wonder what the record will reach to. 
This relates to me and my community because Lebron James continues to be an inspiration to many and he will continue to raise the record of most career points.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I noticed that out of all these legendary players, the player that seems to be grabbing most of the attention due to him overpassing Kareem is LeBron James. This is because as shown on the graph the time frame of LeBron making more points than Kareem is much shorter and he has managed to pass him, meanwhile for Kareem it took a longer amount of time to get close to the amount of points as LeBron. Whereas the current player that has made the lowest amount of career points was Rudy Gay, that's including the fact that he is close to being the same age as LeBron.
What do you wonder?
I wonder if it would be possible for LeBron James to pass Kareem in the career points if he didn't take a break in his career. I also wonder if the NBA is improving when it comes to the quality of the players because based on their stats as time passes by the players just seem to be getting better and better.
How does this relate to you and your community? 
This relates to me and my community because like these NBA players, we have students in the school who play basketball and are ranked or even compared to other basketball players in the district or even in the state where they get to see how well they do throughout their career. Hopefully, someone within this community who is actually good at playing basketball gets to look at the success of these legendary players and are inspired enough to want to do just as well as them.
What's going on in this graph?
The NBA's Rising Stars

raw_comment:
The graph shows that LeBron has overtaken Kareem and is now the player with more points in NBA history career with 38,390; he also overpasses the old record at a younger age. The other current players are very much below him; the closest to Lebron is Curry, who has a difference of proximity of 10,000 points. Since LeBron was around 20 years old, he was at the top of the charts for having the most points per age. 

I wonder if NBA had better quality in the past than now because most players in the graph are retired. Since 34 years had to pass until someone broke Kareem's record, how much time has to run until someone broke LeBron's record? 

This graph relates to my community because we in Perth Amboy have many young people who love to play Basketball, and seeing LeBron breaking records can inspire them to follow their passion. 

New NBA star leads the points record.

1.I notice that each line has a different slope and Lebron James has the highest slope because he reaches the top scoring player earlier than any other player. Another thing I notice is that Lebron James started his career earlier than most of the other players in the graph. This explains why he reaches the top scorer player younger than Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Another important factor I noticed is that compared to player Micheal Jordan, there are no extended periods of time with no growth. 
2.I wonder how the graph would differ if the x and y axis were switched? It took 34 years for James to break Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's record so I wonder if this new record will be broken in a shorter or longer period of time. 
3.This relates to my community because as a black person in America basketball is one of the most influential sports. So Lebron James becomes an inspiration to many of us so as he breaks another record, we can see as a minority in America we can still make a huge difference and obtain major career goals. 
4.LeBron's Journey to NBA Hall of Fame

raw_comment:
1) What do you notice?
I noticed that as the years passed, every player's career points increased. Alongside that, it is evident that Lebron James' career points are highlighted and he has the highest scoring record. His record points are so high that he beat Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's record. He was able to achieve this at a much younger age than everyone else portrayed on the graph.

2) What do you wonder?
I wonder how rules or the sport itself was different which is why some players did not increase in points as much as others did. I am curious to know what motivates some of these players to be their best. I also wonder if anyone will be able to beat Lebron's career points at a quicker pace and sooner than he did. 

3) How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me and my community because many people here look up to Lebron and his accomplishments. He is an inspiration to many and like him, many in my community share a similar story. They come from relatively low income households, but work hard to get the recognition that they deserve.

raw_comment:
1) I've noticed that LeBron's point productivity throughout his career has been significantly quicker and greater than that of other basketball players; additionally, he's acquiring these points at a younger age. Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Karl Malone did not reach their total career points total until the age of 42. Another thing to note is that the line graph indicates areas where there is no growth, such as the line graph for Stephen Curry, which might be due to athletes suffering injuries that impacted their overall career points. 

2) I'm curious if players' chances of competing against LeBron James for the most points in history have been hampered by injuries. How many career points would Kareem Abdul have scored if the three-point line had been in place in the 1980s? Does the graph account for an 82-game season and the break when COVID 19 forced a nationwide lockdown?

3) This is relevant to me and my community because many youngsters of the new generation have observed an athlete who has committed his life to the sport and may serve as an example to many future NBA players. His narrative is similar to that of many students in our community who come from low-income households and are working hard to get recognition in the sports industry and find opportunities to not only support themselves but their family via the sport that they love. 

4) The Crowning of a New King: LeBron James Sweeps the NBA to become the NBA's all-time leading scorer!

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
LeBron James consistently has always had the top Career points by age since the beginning of his career. He has been very consistent and has never fallen below the top all-time Career points by age for the top 250 scorers.
What do you wonder?
Since scoring these large amounts and building up Career points takes many years I wonder when the next time another player will be able to compete with him at any age point. I wonder if someone new could come into the league at a younger age and have a very successful first few years and pass him in the earlier stages of their career in comparison.
How does this relate to you and your community? 
Many people use these statistics along with others to determine who they believe the best player of all time is. This relates to the community of basketball fans and help's support the argument that LeBron James is the top player of all time.

Today’s graph displays a comparison of the extraordinary skill, durability, creativity and talent of LeBron James and other extraordinary players, past and present.  LeBron blasted through  the National Basketball Association (NBA) all-time top scorer record on February 7, 2023.  His point-scoring trajectory continues.

The next “What’s Going On In This Graph?” will be released by Friday, February 17 with moderation in two weeks on Wednesday, March 1.  The topic – the earthquake affecting Turkey and Syria.

I also noticed that Lebron got to pass the number of most points at a much earlier age than Kareem. I also noticed that by the time Lebron James gets to the age of Kareem he would have scored over 40,000 points. raw_comment:
What do you notice? 
When looking at the graph I notice that Lebron James is the top scorer in NBA history with 38,390 points sc0red, just three points above Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. When looking further back into the graph it can actually be seen that Lebron has always had the highest score for his current age in history as well. I also noticed that compared to other players such as Michael Jordan and Stephen Curry, the rate at which James’ points increased was much more consistent.

What do you wonder?
I wonder how Lebron has been able to keep his game so consistent throughout the years and even right now when he’s about to reach forty years old. According to the graph, he doesn’t seem to be getting any worse so I wonder how far he can take the record before he eventually has to retire.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to my community and I because it shows that things that may seem impossible aren’t. When Lebron first started his career, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar held the record for the most points and from 0 points he made it all the way to the current record now at 38,390 points. So the people around me who may have goals that feel impossible can see something like this and feel more inspired and motivated to keep trying to achieve what they want to achieve.

Headline
“King James Reigns Supreme Amongst NBA’s Elite: Top 250 Scorers Announced!”

raw_comment:
1) What do you notice?
In the graph I noticed the positive correlation between age and career points, presumably because as you age you gain more experience to play better. The line for LeBron James notably has the highest slope, showing how he scored higher points in a shorter amount of time/younger ages. Kareem Abdul-Jabar has the longest career on the graph, stopping around 41. I also notice that a majority of the top 250 scorers are not current players.
2) What do you wonder?
I wonder if current players will ever take up half, or even a majority of the graph.
3) How does this relate to you and your community?
Sports are a big part of any community, and especially with so many top scorers being men of color, it relates to my community that has a lot of young non-white athletes. Over time, people are also able to accomplish more at younger ages, which relates to my peers and I who are of a younger generation.
4) What’s going on in this graph?
My headline would be "The Progression of NBA Legends"

This relates to me and my community because someone of color being successful can motivate many others to continue working hard for their dreams, especially the people who want to continue basketball in the future. It could also mean that there could be more good basketball players in the future.

raw_comment:
What do I notice?
The most obvious thing about the graph is that Lebron James has broken records with the highest points In his career at the youngest age. Kareem came in a close second with a similar amount of points only about 4 years after him. Besides this, I also notice the men in the basketball league reaching the high points in their career are incredibly close in age, making 33-38 the most common age for the highest career t points in this graph. 

What do I wonder?
I wonder what about Lebron James makes him different enough to have an unbeatable score. Was it his upbringing? His education/ practice? His team? Or simply his dedication? I also wonder what the grey streaks in the graph represent. Could it be other upcoming players? and what distinguishes the blues from the grey in the chart?

How does this relate to my community and me?
This relates to my community and me because sports, basketball specifically, surround every community. Everyone is interested in who scores the highest points and what team makes it further. Most of the players listed on the diagram are iconic and have been nationally known for years. I personally am not a basketball fan yet those around me stay up to date with graphs like the one presented.

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that players with the highest career points are within the same age demographic, meaning these players are between the ages of 37 to 42. I also noticed that only two people reached the highest career points (with a 34-year gap): LeBron James in 2023 and Kareem Abdul-Jabbur in 1989. 
2. Looking at and analyzing the graph above makes me wonder if there is a proportional relationship between the players' ages and the number of career points they score. Is it possible that the older the players get, the more likely they score high points than someone about a decade younger? Or is there another factor in play that allowed both Lebron and Abdul-Jabbar to achieve the highest career points? 
3. It’s cool not only to witness such an accomplishment but also to say that I was alive when LeBron James scored the highest career points after thirty decades. It feels more relevant and personal because, with Abdul-Jabbar, who achieved the same thing LeBron had, no one in my generation was alive, but that changed with LeBron.  
4. The graph illustrates an increasing trend with ages and career points scored, adding to the evidence that there may be a relationship between the two.

raw_comment:
Lebron is on his way to becoming one of the best basketball players of all time because of his career points and the fact that he was the youngest player to ever reach those points. In the graph, my evidence can be supported on the x-axis where it says different ages. If you look at the plotted points and how Lebron’s line continuously increases you can see that he has scored the most points out of anyone in each age range. 

I wonder if there will ever come a time when someone is able to beat the highest score for career points at a younger age than Lebron did. We know that Lebron has kids who play basketball and there are many more generations to come with basketball prodigies anxious to beat the top scorer. 

This relates to me and my community because there is a lot of youth basketball players and LeBron's accomplishment is a motivator for them to work hard and follow through with their basketball goals to one day be able to beat incrible records that great ledgends have set. 

Timeless: NBA's Leading Career Point Scorer

raw_comment:
1. From the graph, I noticed that as every player in the top 250 scorers gets older, they earn more career points. This age-to-career point ratio is represented by a majority of the lines increasing on the graph. However, there are a few exceptions to this ratio which is represented by the lines that flatline, or stay the same slope, starting from the middle of the graph. These lines indicate that those players, for the remainder of their basketball careers, did not gain any more career points once they reached a certain age. 

2. I wonder why most people thought it was impossible for anyone to beat Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. Society tends to put people down instead of encouraging them to reach their full potential. They should not have doubted LeBron James’ skill at first. 

3. The graph relates to me and my community because it discusses a sport that many people play and enjoy watching. Basketball is a very common sport and can help people discover their true potential. It is also very beneficial mentally and physically. 

4. A catchy headline I would choose to capture this graph’s main idea is “Top 250 Players’ Career Layers.” The reasoning behind this would be that the graph describes the players’ career points which are part of their layers, or characteristics, that make them a part of who they are.

raw_comment:
1. I noticed that there are only a handful of players that have scored over 30,000 career points (all of which no longer currently play in the NBA except for LeBron James).  In addition, I noticed that these handful of players tend to be in their upper-thirties or lower-forties. LeBron James is one of the younger scorers to pass the 30,000 threshold. 
2. I wonder if there will be anyone to pass James’s record in the future, or even come close to it. It was presumed that no one would be able to pass Kareem Abdul Jabbar for highest career points, but that has since been done, so this makes me wonder if anyone years from now will be able to pass LeBron James. 
3. This relates to me because I played basketball for the majority of my life. While my total career points do not nearly come close to anyone on this graph, I still believe my career points were high compared to those at the levels I was playing at. In addition, basketball in general is a commonly discussed topic for people in my school community since our girl’s basketball team is one of the best in the country.
4. New King in Town: LeBron Takes the Crown for Highest Career Points

raw_comment: I noticed that James has the steepest increase in scoring as he has gotten older. He reached more career points than previous record-holder Abdul-Jabbar in less time. LeBron James is the youngest basketball player to reach a career point record of 38,390 points at the age of 38 years old, beating a record after three decades. I wonder if another basketball player in the future will be able to live up to this record-high career point value. Will it take generations of basketball players for someone else to beat this achievement before 38 years old? By LeBron reaching this record last week, it has created a wave of inspiration for many athletes. Getting to witness a living legend is a privilege because it allows athletes all over the globe to watch someone grow to beat a record set by a previous player. Athletes look up to those who set records in the past as motivation to work up to that level one day. We get to look back on LeBron’s journey, as there are films from his high school career all the way to the NBA, and we can watch him reach new limits in live time. The ability to witness history is a gift and an inspiration for many to continue making history in the future, whether it's athletically or within other career areas. Looking at the multiple athletes that have shown exponential career-point growth on the graph, I realize how big of an accomplishment this really is for LeBron, as he breaks a record that has remained for over three decades.

raw_comment: I noticed that LeBron James reached a new record of scoring the most career points out of the top 250 scorers. The evidence supports this claim because the blue line tracking his points is clearly above others. Although it may seem close to Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, the graph clearly states that LeBron James scored 38,390 points while Kareem Abdul-Jabbar only scored 38,397 points. After analyzing the graph, I wonder how many career points LeBron James will account for throughout the entirety of his career. Kareem Abdul-Jabbar was 42 years old when he retired and set the previous record. LeBron James is only 38 years old now when he sets the new record. If he continues to play for a few more years how many more points will he score? Will anyone beat his record? This relates to me and my community because it shows people that someone is always able to create a record. New records motivate thousands of people to work harder just so they can have the highest record. About 34 years ago when the previous record was set, people thought that was the record for life, until, LeBron James came to set the current record. This refers back to the previous article we read where we cannot label someone as the “G.O.A.T.” (Greatest Of All Time) because there will always be someone better in the future. A new headline can be "After 34 years, LeBron James beats Kareem Abdul-Jabbar with the most career points with only more to come in the future."

raw_comment:
Does this graph solidify Lebron James as the best basketball player of all time?
I notice that Lebron James holds the title as the NBA’s career leading scorer. There are also a bunch of names underneath Lebron James with some of the most well-known NBA players of all time. I also notice that the ages of the NBA players are on the x axis and the total career points are on the y axis. My claim would be that Lebron James will pass 50,000 career points by the end of his career. The evidence supports it because the graph shows Lebron is 38 years old and has scored 40,000 career points. The NBA player, Kareem Abdul Jabar, played until he was 42 years old and he has less than Lebron’s career points. Therefore, I believe that in 4 years time Lebron could score 10,000 more career points.
This relates to me specifically because Lebron James has truly been one of my all time favorite athletes. He comes from an incredible background and the fact that he is now the ALL-TIME NBA leading scorer His dedication, hard work, and his overall attitude inspires me to be better and work harder. Lebron James passing this record affects the entire NBA community and gives him an even higher point in the debate of the best basketball player of all time.

raw_comment:
Looking at the graph I notice the small amount of time, compared to other players, that Lebron took to break the scoring record. With the age of the player being on the x-axis and the number of points on the y, we can see just how amazing Lebron James was. The former leader in points took until after the age of 40, unlike Lebron who took the record around the age of 36. I also notice how the graph includes current players such as Stephen Curry, James Harden, Kevin Durant, and Rudy Gay. Lebron, in this graph, is showcasing the utter dominance he held over the NBA leading him to become the all-time scoring leader. This graph makes me wonder what Michael Jordan could have accomplished with a full career. Jordan took a considerable break from the NBA, as shown by the graph, and looks like he would have been on pace to also pass Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. It also makes me wonder if Kevin Durant has a shot of coming in at third on the all-time leaderboard as he is also on pace with Karl Malone and Michael Jordan. The addition of Kobe Bryant also makes me question if he didn’t get hurt could he have possibly passed the record? Per the graph, it seems so as he was extremely close to Lebron James before his long break. 
Lebron James' utter dominance demonstrates why he is the greatest player of all time

raw_comment:
1. Lebron is on his way to becoming one of the best basketball players of all time because of his career points and the fact that he was the youngest player to ever reach those points. In the graph, my evidence can be supported on the x-axis where it says different ages. If you look at the plotted points and how Lebron’s line continuously increases you can see that he has scored the most points out of anyone in each age range. 
2. I wonder if there will ever come a time when someone is able to beat the highest score for career points at a younger age than Lebron did. We know that Lebron has kids who play basketball and there are many more generations to come with basketball prodigies anxious to beat the top scorer. 
3. This relates to me and my community because a lot of my peers keep up with basketball and even idol Lebron James. My family isn’t as big with basketball as they are football but there have been countless times when we have talked about basketball and even Lebron James. My brother actually forced us to watch the newest Space Jam: A New Legacy because Lebron James was in it. So overall this relates to me and my community because it is current events, and it is important to keep up with what’s happening in the world even if it’s just a basketball record. 
4. After an astonishing game against the Oklahoma City Thunder, Lebron James was able to surpass the legendary Kareem Abdul-Jabbar in career-scoring points. What will the 38-year-old do next?

raw_comment:
1. LeBron James has overtaken Kareen Abdul-Jabbar as top scorer with 38,390 career points. He broke this record at a younger age than Abdul-Jabbar did, and is currently still playing, which means this record will only continue to increase and will become more difficult for other players to beat. This graph supports the claim that LeBron James is the best basketball player of our time.

2. I wonder how other players would react to this information. LeBron James joined the NBA at just 18 and has beaten so many other talented players in reaching such a lofty goal. The closest active player to reaching this goal would be Kevin Durant, and according to this graph, Durant has a way to go before he even becomes close to LeBron’s stats. I’m assuming this information would be a motivating force to push players harder in order to break James’ record.

3. While I don’t follow the NBA myself, I know several fans who have watched LeBron James from the beginning of his career. This record is astounding and would be celebratory to any of his fans who have supported him since his young start of just 18 years old. This record settles the debate surrounding the best player of all time, supporting that LeBron James now takes that top spot.

4. LeBron James is now top scorer within the NBA, breaking Kareem Abdul-Jabbar’s record of 38,387 points. Is this enough proof that LeBron James the best player of all time?

raw_comment:
Basketball: The Older, the Better- 
I notice that as basketball players get older, the higher their career points were. LeBron James for instance at 23 had roughly over 10k points whereas at 36 he had 35k points. As for the other players, there is the same linear association as well. I wonder if there will ever be a player who has a dramatic increase that changes the slope of the line. What would you have to do, training wise, to change your point growth perception. Also, what are the outside factors that make LeBron James slope so much steeper than Stephen Curry or Ruby Gay? Were they taller or had more training, etc. This relates to my community because in my high school teams basketball program, you can see that as a freshman, even the best players have lower career points than they did their senior year. Their points add up over time, so obviously they are going to have more points when they are older. So overall, in this graph, it is comparing top scorers career points by age. As the basketball players age, the more points they will have racked up.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I noticed that the majority of the athletes scored higher points as they grew older. For instance, Michael Jordan, Karl Malone, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, and a few other players are the most experienced and have amassed the most points. I also saw that a few players, including Kobe Bryant and LeBron James, who are still a few years younger than the older players but have scored just as much as them. The Goat Graph

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

At the time of the record break, Lebron only broke the record by 3 points. We believe this line is going to increase quite a bit, in the time that Lebron has left in he NBA. The players cannot lose points; they can only go up. A lot of the other players seem like they're a lot lower; we don't think they can catch up. 

What do you wonder?

Could a player's points go down, if they shot baskets in the other team's hoop?

raw_comment:
I noticed that as most of the players got older, they scored more points. For example, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Karl Malone, Michael Jordan, and a few other players are the oldest and they have scored the most points. I also noticed that a few players, like Kobe Bryant and LeBron James, have scored just as much as the older players but are still younger than them by a couple years. No one that is LeBron's age has come close to scoring as many points as him.

I wonder if some of the younger players will beat LeBron's record as they get older? I also wonder what the slope of these lines are? I think it would be interesting to see how many points each player scores each year on average.

This relates to me and my community because my family and I enjoy watching basketball. I am also a big Stephen Curry fan so it is interesting to see that he has scored a lot of points compared to other people his age.

"is LeBron James the greatest of all time??"

raw_comment:
1. I've noticed that LeBron James has scored the most career points of any player at a much younger age than the others. The only other player to come close to that number of points was Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, who played in 1989 but did so at a much later age. All of the other players who came close to those points were in their late 30s or early 40s. LeBron James and a few others have significantly more points than the average basketball player.

2. I'm curious if anything has changed in the sport since the early decades when it was played. Sports, whether it's the rules of the games, the physique of the players, the number of games played, or the circumstances and extra factors, usually evolve as generations pass and better ways of playing it are discovered. So, has anything changed in basketball to allow LeBron to break a record held by a much older and more experienced player?

3. Many people in my community enjoy discussing who the best basketball player is. This graph depicts the statistics, and despite the fact that it is based on facts, many people would disagree that LeBron is the best player.

4. "IS LEBRON TRULY KING OF THE COURT?"
